## IV CLAIMS UNDER THE INHERITANCE (PROVISION FOR FAMILY AND DEPENDANTS) ACT 1975

## Scope of this section

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > Scope of this section] 57.14 This Section contains rules about claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975 6 (‘the Act’). ## Proceedings in the High Court

## 57.15

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (1) Proceedings in the High Court under the Act shall be issued in either –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (a) the Chancery Division; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (b) the Family Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (2) The Civil Procedure Rules apply to proceedings under the Act which are brought in the Family Division, except that the provisions of the Family Proceedings Rules 2010 7 relating to the drawing up and service of orders apply instead of the provisions in Part 40 and Practice Direction 40B. ## Procedure for claims under section 1 of the Act

## 57.16

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (1) A claim under section 1 of the Act must be made by issuing a claim form in accordance with Part 8. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (2) Rule 8.3 (acknowledgment of service) and rule 8.5 (filing and serving written evidence) apply as modified by paragraphs (3) to (5) of this rule. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3) The written evidence filed and served by the claimant with the claim form must, except in the circumstances specified in paragraph (3A), have exhibited to it an official copy of –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) the grant of probate or letters of administration in respect of the deceased’s estate; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) every testamentary document in respect of which probate or letters of administration were granted. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3A) Where no grant has been obtained, the claimant may make a claim without naming a defendant and may apply for directions as to the representation of the estate. The written evidence must—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) explain the reasons why it has not been possible for a grant to be obtained;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) be accompanied by the original or a copy (if either is available) of the will or other testamentary document in respect of which probate or letters of administration are to be granted; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (c) contain the following information, so far as known to the claimant—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (i) brief details of the property comprised in the estate, with an approximate estimate of its capital value and any income that is received from it;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (ii) brief details of the liabilities of the estate;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (iii) the names and addresses of the persons who are in possession of the documents relating to the estate; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (iv) the names of the beneficiaries and their respective interests in the estate. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3B) Where a claim is made in accordance with paragraph (3A), the court may give directions as to the parties to the claim and as to the representation of the estate either on the claimant’s application or on its own initiative. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (Section 4 of the 1975 Act as amended confirms that nothing prevents the making of an application under the Act before representation with respect to the estate of the deceased person is taken out.)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (4) Subject to paragraph (4A), the time within which a defendant must file and serve –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) any written evidence,

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] is not more than 21 days after service of the claim form on him. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (4A) If the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.32 or 6.33, the period for filing an acknowledgment of service and any written evidence is 7 days longer than the relevant period specified in rule 6.35 or Practice Direction 6B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (5) A defendant who is a personal representative of the deceased must file and serve written evidence, which must include the information required by Practice Direction 57. ## V PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PRESUMPTION OF DEATH ACT 2013

## Scope and interpretation

## 57.17

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.17] (1) This Section contains rules about proceedings under the Presumption of Death Act 2013. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.17] (2) In this Section, terms used in the Presumption of Death Act 2013 Act have the meaning given by that Act, and—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.17] (a) ‘the 2013 Act’ means the Presumption of Death Act 2013;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.17] (b) ‘a claim for a declaration of presumed death’ means a claim under section 1 of the 2013 Act for a declaration that a missing person is presumed to be dead;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.17] (c) ‘a claim for a variation order’ means a claim for an order under section 5 of the 2013 Act varying or revoking a declaration of presumed death. ## Proceedings to be in the High Court

## 57.18

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.18] (1) Proceedings under the 2013 Act must be issued in the High Court in either—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.18] (a) the Chancery Division; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.18] (b) the Family Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.18] (2) The Civil Procedure Rules apply to proceedings under the 2013 Act which are brought in the Family Division, except that the provisions of the Family Procedure Rules 2010(a) relating to the drawing up and service of orders apply instead of the provisions in Part 40 and Practice Direction 40B. ## Procedure for claims for a declaration of presumed death or a variation order

## 57.19

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (1) A claim for a declaration of presumed death or for a variation order must be made by issuing a claim form in accordance with Part 8. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (2) In addition to the matters set out in rule 8.2 (contents of the claim form), the claim form must also include or be accompanied by the information required by Practice Direction 57B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (3) Rules 8.2A, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 apply as modified by paragraphs (4) to (7) of this rule (and references elsewhere in these Rules to a defendant and to an acknowledgment of service are, where relevant, to be read as references to the substitute terms in rules 8.2A, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 as so modified). [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (4) Rule 8.2A (issue of claim form without naming defendants) applies as if for ‘without naming a defendant’ in paragraph (1) there were substituted ‘without serving notice on any person’. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (5) Rule 8.3 (acknowledgment of service) applies—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (a) as if, instead of referring to a defendant, it referred to a person giving notice of intention to intervene or applying for permission to intervene, as the case may be;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (b) as if, instead of referring to an acknowledgment of service, it referred to a notice of intention to intervene or an application for permission to intervene, as the case may be; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (c) subject to paragraph (7), with the substitution of 21 days for 14 days as the time within which the notice of intention to intervene or application for permission to intervene must be filed and served. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (6) Rules 8.4 (consequence of not filing an acknowledgment of service) and 8.5 (filing and serving written evidence) apply—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (a) as if, instead of referring to a defendant, they referred to a person giving notice of intention to intervene or applying for permission to intervene, as the case may be; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (b) as if, instead of referring to an acknowledgment of service, they referred to a notice of intention to intervene or an application for permission to intervene, as the case may be. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.19] (7) If the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.32 or 6.33, the period for filing notice of intention to intervene or an application for permission to intervene, as the case may be, and any written evidence, is 7 days longer than the relevant period for serving an acknowledgement of service specified in rule 6.35 or Practice Direction 6B. ## Giving notice of claim

## 57.20

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (1) Where the claim is for a declaration of presumed death, the claimant must give notice of the claim by serving a copy of it on the following persons (where not the claimant)—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (a) the spouse or civil partner of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (b) any parent of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (c) any child of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (d) any sibling of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (e) if there are no persons within sub-paragraphs (a) to (d), the nearest relative of the missing person known to the claimant; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (f) any other person (including in particular any insurance company) appearing to the claimant to have an interest in the claim. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (2) Where the claim is for a variation order, the claimant must give notice of the claim by serving a copy of it on the following persons (where not the claimant)—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (a) the person who was the claimant for the declaration of presumed death or (as the case may be) previous variation order which it is sought to have varied or revoked;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (b) the spouse or civil partner of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (c) any parent of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (d) any child of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (e) any sibling of the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (f) if there are no persons within sub-paragraphs (b) to (e), the nearest relative of the missing person known to the claimant; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (g) any other person (including in particular any insurance company) appearing to the claimant to have an interest in the claim. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.20] (3) Notice under paragraph (1)(a) to (f) or paragraph (2)(a) to (g) must be given within 7 days after the claim is issued. ## Advertisement of claim

## 57.21

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.21] (1) The claimant (whether the claim is for a declaration of presumed death or for a variation order) must, within 7 days of issue of the claim, ensure that notice of the claim is published—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.21] (a) in a form which meets the requirements set out in Practice Direction 57B; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.21] (b) in at least one newspaper circulating in the vicinity of the last known address of the missing person. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.21] (2) The claimant must, at least 5 days before the hearing, file a copy of the page of the newspaper bearing the advertisement of notice of the claim required by paragraph (1) and the date on which it was published. ## Interveners

## 57.22

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.22] (1) The Attorney General, or a person who is entitled to intervene in proceedings under section 11(1), must first notify the court of the intention to intervene in accordance with the requirements of Practice Direction 57B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.22] (2) Any other person who wishes to intervene in such proceedings must submit an application for permission to intervene in accordance with the requirements of Practice Direction 57B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.22] (3) Where the court grants permission to intervene, it may do so on conditions and may give case management directions. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.22] (4) The court may direct that a person who intervenes in proceedings, other than the Attorney General, be joined as a claimant or defendant. ## Requirement to provide information

## 57.23

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (1) An application for an order under section 12(1) of the 2013 Act must be supported by evidence and must in particular—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (a) specify or describe the information in respect of which the order is sought;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (b) set out the reasons why the person making the application believes that the person against whom the order is sought is likely to have such information; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (c) include any further details, where known, of the missing person which are likely to assist in providing the information sought. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (2) The person making the application must serve a copy of the application notice on the person against whom the order is sought, and on every other party to the proceedings (within the meaning of section 20(2) of the 2013 Act), at least 14 days before the date fixed for the hearing of the application. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.23] (3) An application for discharge or variation under section 12(6) of an order made under section 12(1) may be made without notice unless the court directs otherwise. ## Requirement to send copy of declaration to the Public Guardian

## 57.24

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.24] Where a declaration of presumed death made under the 2013 Act satisfies section 3(3)(a) or (b) of that Act, the court must send a copy of the declaration to the Public Guardian. ## SECTION VI PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE GUARDIANSHIP (MISSING PERSONS) ACT 2017

## Scope and interpretation

## 57.25

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (1) This Section contains rules about proceedings under the Guardianship (Missing Persons) Act 2017. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (2) In this Section, terms used in the Guardianship (Missing Persons) Act 2017 have the meaning given by that Act, and—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (a) “the 2017 Act” means the Guardianship (Missing Persons) Act 2017;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (b) “the missing person” means the person who is or has been asserted to be “missing” within the meaning of the 2017 Act;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (c) “a claim for a guardianship order” means an application under section 2 (applying for a guardianship order) of the 2017 Act for a guardianship order;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (d) “an application for a revocation/variation order” means—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (i) an application under section 12 (variation of a guardianship order) of the 2017 Act for an order varying a guardianship order; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (ii) an application under section 13 (revocation of a guardianship order) of the 2017 Act for an order revoking a guardianship order;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (e) “an application relating to a guardianship order” means any application which relates to the exercise of functions of a guardian but which is not a claim for a guardianship order or an application for a revocation/variation of a guardianship order;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.25] (f) “an intervener” means either a person who falls within section 21(1) of the 2017 Act and who has given notice of intention to intervene, or a person to whom the court has given permission to intervene. ## Proceedings to be in the High Court

## 57.26

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.26] (1) Proceedings under the 2017 Act must be issued in the High Court in either—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.26] (a) the Chancery Division; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.26] (b) the Family Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.26] (2) The Civil Procedure Rules apply to proceedings under the 2017 Act which are brought in the Family Division, except that in the Family Division the provisions of Part 29 of the Family Procedure Rules 2010(a) relating to the drawing up and service of orders shall apply instead of the provisions in the Civil Procedure Rules Part 40 and Practice Direction 40B. ## Procedure for making claims for a guardianship order

## 57.27

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (1) A claim for a guardianship order must be made by issuing a claim form in accordance with Part 8. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (2) Following issue, the court shall fix a date for the first hearing of the claim and which shall, unless the court otherwise orders, be not less than 56 days from the date of issue; but any person may apply for the claim or an application to be heard at an earlier date. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (3) In addition to the matters set out in rule 8.2 (contents of the claim form), the claim form must also include the information required by paragraph 1.1 of Practice Direction 57C and be accompanied by a witness statement containing the information required by paragraph 1.2 and, where appropriate, paragraph 1.3 of Practice Direction 57C. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (4) The claim form must name the missing person as the defendant but—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (a) the claimant need take no steps to serve the claim form upon the missing person unless the court orders otherwise;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (b) the court shall consider at the first hearing what, if any, directions to make regarding service or dispensing with service of the claim form upon the missing person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (c) Rules 6.9, 6.15, 6.16 and 7.5 (rules as to service of the claim form) shall not apply. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.27] (5) Rules 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (rules relating to part 8 claims) shall not apply. (Rule 57.29 sets out further steps that a claimant must take.)

## 57.28

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (1) An application for a revocation/variation order and an application relating to a guardianship order must be made in accordance with Part 23 as modified by this rule and by paragraph 2 of Practice Direction 57C. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (2) In addition to the matters set out in rule 23.6 (what an application notice must include), the application notice must also include, or be accompanied by, a witness statement which contains the information required by paragraph 2 of Practice Direction 57C in relation to that type of application. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (3) Following issue, the court shall fix a date for the first hearing of the application which shall, unless the court otherwise orders, be not less than 56 days from the date of issue; but any person may apply for the application to be heard at an earlier date. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (4) The applicant need take no steps to serve the application or any order upon the missing person unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (5) Rules 23.9 and 23.11 apply as modified by paragraphs (6) and (7). [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (6) Rule 23.9(2) (service of application where application made without notice) applies as if it did not refer to the missing person as defendant, but did refer also to any interveners. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.28] (7) Rule 23.11 (power of court to proceed in the absence of a party) applies as if the words “or any intervener” were inserted after both references to “any respondent”.
